H1.note: IL12B composes to Crohn via IL-23 signaling and IL-17 production. The IL23R claim has no route: the chain represents IL23R only as the receptor-activation process (Reactome IL-23 signaling), not as the IL23R protein node.

H2.note: Both genes act by loss of function (NOD2 frameshift, LACC1/FAMIN loss-of-function risk alleles), so sign neg. LACC1 composes to Crohn via innate-immune clearance. NOD2 has no route: it never appears as a statement subject (only inside the GO:0070431 label and as evidence).

H3.no_claim_reason: the run leaves GPR35's net direction on Crohn explicitly unresolved (opposite Gpr35 knockout colitis models and both risk and protective alleles), so there is no directional claim to compose

findings.detail: 'bacterial muramyl dipeptide' is grounded to CHEBI:6791, which is metamitron (a triazine herbicide), not muramyl dipeptide; the correct term is CHEBI:59414.

Several chain nodes carry the wrong kind: muramyl dipeptide and the kynurenic-acid metabolites are tagged kind 'gene' (they are chemicals), and LACC1 (Q8IV20) and GPR35 (Q9HC97) proteins are tagged kind 'process'.

H1.2 grounds its object to GO:2000330 (Th17 commitment) while H1.3's subject is GO:0032740 (IL-17 production); they are different nodes, so the chain connects only after the compound object 'T-helper 17 lineage commitment and IL-17 production' is split to expose GO:0032740.

H2.1 ends at NOD2 signaling / autophagy (GO:0070431 / GO:0006914) and H2.2 starts at LACC1 (Q8IV20); the steps share no node, so the NOD2 (sensing) half of H2 never connects to the LACC1 -> clearance -> Crohn half.

The terminal '-> Crohn' steps have a process subject (IL-17 inflammation; microbial clearance), but every citation is a variant/gene/Open-Targets/expression record about the genes, so the run's strongest genetics (NOD2 frameshift OR ~3.1, IL23R OR 2.66) supports no composable statement.

H1 and H2 each name two genes but represent one of each as a process: IL23R as the Reactome receptor-activation pathway and NOD2 only inside a process label; so the IL23R and NOD2 protein claims have no route while the IL12B and LACC1 claims do.

H3's contradicting_evidence lists three Gpr35-knockout colitis annotations, but two (MP:0013299, MP:0008539: knockout decreases colitis) indicate GPR35 is harmful and so agree with the hypothesis; only MP:0008537 (knockout increases colitis) truly opposes it.

H1.1 and H1.2 cite STRING GO-set enrichment and a Reactome pathway over-representation as mechanistic steps, but over-representation states co-membership of the input genes, not a directional causal link.
H3.1's subject 'microbial/host metabolites including kynurenic acid and 5-HIAA' is a compound of ligands grounded only to kynurenic acid (CHEBI:18344); 5-HIAA was dropped.
The only STRING link between NOD2 and LACC1 (combined 0.70) is text-mining only (experimental 0.00, database 0.00), yet it is used to justify a direct NOD2-LACC1 coupling edge.

The run's object labels are multi-part ('NOD2-RIPK2 signaling and autophagy'; 'optimal NOD2 cytokine signaling, autophagy, and bacterial clearance'; 'altered chemokines, interleukins, leukocyte recruitment, and epithelial injury') yet each is grounded to one GO term; the format cannot mark that a single term stands for an umbrella, so curation must choose split vs umbrella per step.

The run abstains on MEIS1 and TRIM4 with grounded reasoning, but curated.json has no slot for an abstention (not a hypothesis with claims, not a finding), and the abstention's cited accessions (GWAS:MEIS1:no-association, OT:MEIS1-..., O00470, Q9C037, CXG:...) are absent from sources.json so they cannot be checked.
H1.3's disease target names both susceptibility and activity ('Crohn disease susceptibility and activity'), but a disease target carries one aspect; curated as risk.

For an unsigned (direction none) association there is no clean slot for conflicting signed mechanistic evidence; the opposing mouse Gpr35 knockout results were recorded as one refutes plus two 'other' exclusions on S10, which the guide's refutes/exclude rule handles only awkwardly.

Two H1 supporting-only citations are cited by no chain step and state no composable statement: CHEMBL:CHEMBL1201835 (ustekinumab targets IL12B, clinical stage APPROVAL) and PMID:17068223 (the original GWAS associating IL23R with Crohn); the chain's terminal step has a process subject, so the run's approved-drug and founding-GWAS evidence attaches nowhere and is lost.

Two H2 supporting-only citations are cited by no chain step and state no composable statement: PMID:40089498 (Crohn-risk LACC1 promoter variants lower LACC1 in CD4 T cells and alter T-cell metabolism) and CXG:ENSG00000179630:CL_0000235:MONDO_0005011 (LACC1 detected in more Crohn than normal colon macrophages, an expression difference only).

audit.before: No handling of H1's supporting-only citations CHEMBL:CHEMBL1201835 (ustekinumab, APPROVAL) and PMID:17068223 (IL23R GWAS); neither appears in any evidence/excluded list nor as a finding.
audit.after: Added a citation_at_no_step finding for H1 naming both citations.
audit.reason: The guide requires supporting citations no step cites to be attached where they state a step, otherwise recorded as a citation_at_no_step finding. Neither states a composable step (the chain's terminal step has a process subject), so a finding is the correct handling. The approved anti-IL12B drug is the run's strongest clinical evidence and had no home.

audit.before: No handling of H2's supporting-only citations PMID:40089498 (LACC1 T-cell variant mechanism) and CXG:ENSG00000179630:CL_0000235:MONDO_0005011 (LACC1 macrophage expression difference); neither appears in any evidence/excluded list nor as a finding.
audit.after: Added a citation_at_no_step finding for H2 naming both citations.
audit.reason: Same guide rule: supporting citations cited by no step must be attached or recorded as a finding. Neither states a composable step (S7's subject is LACC1 into a clearance process; these are a T-cell mechanism and an expression difference), so a finding is correct.
